A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with matching authors, central propositions, and experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic Transformer experiments, including training convergence, logit comparisons, and KL-divergence results in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain these original experimental results, now displayed in Figures 2–5.

M1.justification: The ARM/EBM mappings, training objectives, causal and non-causal Transformer architectures, and sampling procedures are unchanged. Renaming the sequence score from Q_q to R_q changes notation only.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic sequence spaces, V=8 with T=4 and V=4 with T=8, and the same Zipfian and softargmax-normal target distributions. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons remain causal ARMs versus non-causal EBMs and logit comparisons before and after the same mapping. The additional cited works do not participate as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains full enumeration of 4,096 or 65,536 sequences, the same two- and three-layer configurations, Adam schedule and learning-rate search, and optimality-gap, logit-distance, and KL metrics.

E4.justification: Appendices C.4–C.5 retain the same model-size and vocabulary/length comparisons, mapping analysis, and investigation of KL versus logit distance under concentrated target distributions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting and the experimental figures, including their visible variability, are unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, confidence-interval reporting, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: V1 Figures 1–4 reappear as v2 Figures 2–5 with identical plotted results. The convergence findings and the observation that KL can approach zero while logit distance remains nonzero are retained.

T1.justification: The propositions, bounds, assumptions, and appendix derivations remain substantively unchanged. V2 explicitly restates bijectivity in Proposition 1 and notes the already-derived inverse in Appendix B.2; the terminal-reward construction moves into B.3. These changes clarify existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: function-space ARM/EBM equivalence, its soft-Bellman connection, teacher-forcing optimality in that setting, and KL bounds for distillation.

C2.justification: The explanations of lookahead, optimization and approximation limitations, and concentrated-distribution behavior are retained. The revised computational-cost paragraph reiterates the existing Section 4.1 explanation that supervised learning does not require explicit conversion.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same Flax pseudocode, architecture specifications, data-distribution construction, optimizer settings, and metric computations. No implementation or resource-access information is substantively added or revised.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bengio et al. (2003), Hu et al. (2023), and Foster et al. (2024), including a brief connection to behavior-cloning sample complexity. It removes Todorov (2008) and the Kalman-duality aside. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and notation edits, renames Section 3.2, shortens recursive examples, and adds an impact statement. It also duplicates the References section. The main narrative and appendix organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds a conceptual mapping diagram as Figure 1 and renumbers the unchanged experimental figures. Equation displays and pagination are adjusted. The complete bibliography is printed twice across pages 9–13, introducing substantial local redundancy without redesigning the research displays.

improvement.justification: The new mapping diagram, clearer function-space wording, and additional related-work context offer modest expository benefits. However, v2 duplicates the entire bibliography, introducing an editorial defect absent from v1. With the theory, experiments, and reproducibility information substantively unchanged, these competing presentation effects do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
